prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what you need (realistic human presenters vs. stylized visuals, short social ads vs. longer explainers, budget, languages, integrations, etc.). Below are the top contenders (as of mid‑2024), when to pick each, plus quick pros/cons to help you choose.

Top picks and when to use them
- Synthesia
  - Best for: professional-looking ads with AI human presenters (multi‑language).
  - Pros: realistic avatars, many languages, easy script-to-video, enterprise features and brand kit.
  - Cons: less flexible for custom visual effects; cost scales with seats and minutes.

- HeyGen (formerly Movio) / Elai.io
  - Best for: lower-cost presenter videos and quick localized ads.
  - Pros: good avatar quality, fast turnaround, affordable tiers.
  - Cons: slightly less polish than premium Synthesia avatars.

- InVideo
  - Best for: social media ads, fast template-based video creation.
  - Pros: tons of templates, easy editing, stock assets, good for teams on a budget.
  - Cons: templates can be limiting for highly bespoke creative.

- Lumen5
  - Best for: turning blog posts/scripts into short social videos.
  - Pros: automated scene generation, captioning, quick workflow.
  - Cons: creative control can be limited compared to a full editor.

- Pictory
  - Best for: repurposing long-form content (webinars/podcasts) into short ads.
  - Pros: auto-highlights, subtitle generation, great for content teams.
  - Cons: not for heavy motion-graphics work.

- Runway
  - Best for: advanced generative visuals and high-end creative ads.
  - Pros: cutting-edge generative video tools, compositing and inpainting.
  - Cons: steeper learning curve, higher compute cost for complex outputs.

- VEED / Clipchamp / Canva Video
  - Best for: DIY marketers who want simple editing + some AI features.
  - Pros: cheap or free tiers, easy UI, good for teams that already use these platforms.
  - Cons: fewer advanced AI features than dedicated generators.

- Promo.com / Shakr
  - Best for: e-commerce and performance ad templates built for social platforms.
  - Pros: ad-focused templates, platform ad specs, A/B testing assets.
  - Cons: less generative flexibility.

- Descript + ElevenLabs (combo)
  - Best for: precise editing, voiceover quality, and podcast-to-video workflows.
  - Pros: Descript’s editing and overdub + ElevenLabs realistic TTS = great voiceovers and edits.
  - Cons: more of a do-it-yourself pipeline vs. one-click ad maker.

How to pick the best one for you
- Need a human presenter (multi-language): Synthesia or HeyGen.
- Need fast, cheap social ads with templates: InVideo, Lumen5, Promo.com.
- Repurposing long videos to short ads: Pictory or Opus Clip.
- Want high-end, creative visuals or generative effects: Runway or Kaiber.
- Tight budget/free plan: Canva Video, Clipchamp, VEED.
- Need commercial/agency licensing and enterprise controls: check Synthesia, HeyGen, and enterprise tiers of major platforms.

If you want one recommendation for most small businesses: try InVideo (best balance of templates, speed and price) — or Synthesia if you specifically want AI presenters.

If you tell me:
- your budget,
- primary platform (TikTok, Meta, YouTube),
- ad length,
- whether you want an AI presenter or just animated/stock footage,
I’ll recommend 2–3 specific tools and which plan to start with, plus a short workflow for producing a high-converting ad.
